This card chooses which page the tablet shows and when it reloads. A switch saves immediately. A URL or number saves when the field loses focus. Hours show only the current value. Tap to choose 0 to 23, then confirm to save. Cancel leaves the value unchanged. An invalid value is marked and is not stored.

The home URL must be a full address starting with http:// or https://. The first-run placeholder is http://homeassistant.local:8123/. Change it to your own page.

Idle reload is counted in hours. After that long with no touch, the page reloads once. If nobody touches it, it keeps reloading on the same interval. 0 turns it off. The allowed range is 0 to 720. The default is 12.

Failed-load retry shows a local waiting screen, then tries the current page again after the given seconds. 0 still retries every 30 seconds while that screen is showing. The allowed range is 0 to 3600. The default is 30. Choose dashboard uses the Home Assistant in the home URL and a long-lived access token to list Lovelace dashboards.

Unresponsive reload: if loading never finishes, or the page script stops answering, the tablet clears the cache and returns home after the given seconds. 0 turns it off. The allowed range is 0 to 3600. The default is 0. It does not run while settings are open.

Daily reload is off by default. Turn it on, tap the hour to choose 0 to 23, then confirm. Cancel leaves it unchanged. Enter the minute from 0 to 59. It reloads once at that time and only once that day. The default time is 03:00. It does not run during that minute while settings are open.

Reload now clears the cache, reloads the current page, and closes settings. Go home opens the saved home URL and does not change it.

This card controls brightness and presence. Percent sliders save when released. Numbers save when the field loses focus. Switches save immediately. Hours show only the current value. Tap to choose 0 to 23, then confirm to save. Cancel leaves the value unchanged.

Watch brightness is used while someone is present, from 1 to 100, default 70. Standby brightness is used after the room is empty, from 0 to 100, where 0 is darkest, default 20.

Dim delay: after nobody has been present for the given seconds, standby brightness is used. 0 keeps watch brightness. The allowed range is 0 to 86400. The default is 60.

Brightness by time is off by default. When it is on, a present person gets the day or night level. Day start and night start are hours from 0 to 23, default 7 and 22. Day and night brightness are both 1 to 100, default 70 and 30. After the dim delay with nobody present, standby brightness is still used.

Night screen off is off by default. When it is on, the screen turns off between the start and end hours if nobody is present and settings are closed. Leaving that period turns the screen on again. The same start and end hour never turns the screen off. A start later than the end crosses midnight. The default is 23 to 7. Screen off requires this app to be the device owner.

Motion detection uses the front camera to see whether the picture changes. Frames are analyzed on the tablet only. They are not saved or uploaded. Detection can still wake the screen after it is off. Sensitivity is 0 to 100, and 0 turns detection off. The default is 50. Presence hold is how many seconds someone stays present after motion, from 1 to 3600, default 10. If camera permission is missing, use the grant button below.

This card only sets the tablet media volume, from 0 to 100, default 70. The slider saves when released and writes the system media volume immediately.\n\nRemote playback is not on this card. Play audio and speak commands from MQTT or the LAN API use this media volume.

This connects to an MQTT broker, not to the Home Assistant web address. Put the web address in the home URL on the Page card.

The host is the IP address or domain of the machine running the broker, for example 192.168.1.10. Do not include http:// or a path. The port defaults to 1883 and may be 1 to 65535. The username and password are the broker account. Leave both blank when the broker has no authentication.

The base topic defaults to home_kiosk. The discovery prefix defaults to homeassistant and must match the discovery prefix of the MQTT integration in Home Assistant.

After you turn on Enable MQTT and register with Home Assistant, the tablet registers one device with MQTT Discovery. In Chinese the device name is HA 智能面板. In English it is HAPanel. A state interval of 0 publishes only when something changes. A value above 0 also publishes on that many seconds. The allowed range is 0 to 86400. The default is 60. Switches save immediately. Text saves when the field loses focus.

When the MQTT line at the top of settings says connected, open this device in Home Assistant. You can see screen, presence, battery, brightness, the current URL, CPU, memory, storage, and battery temperature. You can also reload, go home, open a page, set brightness, turn the screen off, take a screenshot, show a notice, speak, set the volume, and play audio. Motion detection, night screen off, daily reload, and the page watchdog can be changed there too. Reboot appears only when this app is the device owner.

If it does not connect, check the MQTT line at the top: off, connected, or not connected. After Home Assistant restarts, the tablet publishes the registration again.

When this is on, the tablet serves a plain HTTP admin API on this device. The default port is 2323. You may use 1024 to 65535. Only this device and LAN addresses are accepted. Other sources are rejected. The switch saves immediately. The port and password save when the field loses focus.

The password must be at least 8 characters. Put it only in a header: Authorization: Bearer followed by the password you set, or the X-Kiosk-Password header. Do not put the password in the URL.

Common calls: GET /status, POST /reload, POST /wake, POST /home, POST /url, POST /brightness, POST /screen-off, POST /play, and POST /reboot. Screen off and reboot need device owner, otherwise the tablet returns 409. A wrong password returns 401.

The card shows this tablet address below the fields. The API is plain HTTP and is meant for a home LAN.

Device owner is the Android management role given to this app. After it is set, the app can use lock task (blocking Home, recents, and the status bar), stay as the home app, grant the camera permission, disable the keyguard, turn the screen off at night, and reboot from MQTT or the LAN API.

Until then, lock task has no effect. Remove every account on the tablet, then run the command printed on this card from a computer. It has the form adb shell dpm set-device-owner followed by this app admin component. The app cannot remove device owner afterward. Only a factory reset can.

While lock task is on, system settings cannot be opened. Turn lock task off and let it save first.

The settings password only protects the panel opened by a swipe from the left edge. It is not the MQTT password and not the LAN password.

It is not saved when a field loses focus. Only Save password writes it. A saved password is not filled back into the fields.

When no password is saved: leave the new password and the repeat blank, then tap Save password to keep the panel unlocked. To enable one, enter the same 4 to 8 digits in both fields, then tap Save password.

When a password is already saved: enter the current password first. Leave the new password and the repeat blank, then tap Save password to remove it. To change it, the current password must be correct and both new fields must match as 4 to 8 digits.

Battery optimization whitelist reduces the chance that the system stops the background connection. Allow it once in the system prompt. Allow open on boot: if this app is not the device owner, allow display over other apps so the dashboard can open after boot. That button hides once the app is the device owner. Allow reading the Wi-Fi name so the status can show it. Open system settings enters Android settings. Lock task blocks that until lock task is off. Buttons for permissions you already granted are hidden.
